title: Cross-depth pairs supplied all depth-group count excess at matched M5.5 selection in global ComCat, 2001-2024
abstract: We tested the meaning of depth-group before and after counts with equal event selection. We used 11,782 ComCat earthquakes of preferred magnitude 5.5 or more in 2001-2024. The primary pair rule used a 200 km hypocentral chord and a time gap of 1 to below 30 days. There were 17,770 chronological pairs. The shallow after-minus-before count was +16. All of it came from 231 shallow-first and 215 intermediate-first pairs. Same-group pairs canceled exactly. The intermediate and deep net counts were -14 and -2. The shallow sign changed with a 100 km radius or an 80 km depth cutoff. We give an exact group identity and an audited aggregate benchmark. The result does not measure causal aftershocks or disprove known depth effects on mainshock productivity. Catalog revision, mixed magnitude types, location error and boundary choices limit empirical interpretation. No population confidence claim is made.

display.caption: Left: counts of chronological depth pairs within 200 km in three dimensions and 1 to below 30 days. Rows give the earlier event group. Colors show log10(1+count); labels show exact counts. Right: shallow after-minus-before counts for all 12 rules. These are descriptive counts, not independent estimates or confidence intervals. A cutoff check changes the shallow group definition.

citations.reason: We extend its pooled reciprocal-pair identity to depth-group matrices. Same ComCat snapshot; not independent confirmation.
Its depth comparison and warning about within-group cancellation motivate our exact group decomposition. Different catalog and equal selection here.
